text: Active geo-replication keeps a readable secondary copy of OverlookDB current in another region. But it leaves a real problem open: how does the scheduling application know which region is currently primary? A failover group adds exactly what's missing — one stable DNS name Azure always points at the current primary.

There's no CREATE FAILOVER GROUP in T-SQL — it's a server-level Azure resource, created with New-AzSqlDatabaseFailoverGroup. Overlook's primary server, a partner server in another region, an automatic failover policy, and a one-hour grace period all get specified in that single command.

Add-AzSqlDatabaseToFailoverGroup then adds OverlookDB itself to the group. The grace period is a deliberate trade-off against Lesson 11's RTO target — a shorter grace period gets closer to a fast recovery, at the cost of a higher chance of reacting to a brief, false alarm.

After this runs, the scheduling application connects to one stable listener endpoint, never the individual server names — the application code never needs to know which region is currently primary. Next lesson actually tests this under a real failover.
